messages:
laura_support: FYI — customer report: acct_9XY lost ~62k free-trial credits overnight. They only ran a scheduled embeddings ingest and applied a promo earlier today. Can someone triage?

sam_ops: thanks, forwarding their ticket. Do we have request_ids/time window?

laura_support: Window per customer: 2026-03-15T00:30:00Z → 2026-03-15T03:15:00Z. They pasted a bunch of request ids in the ticket; top ones look like req_9a1, req_9a2, req_9a3. They say the ingest job retries on 429s and the client uses tenacity (exponential backoff).

jihoon_eng: pinging ingest-bot to pull the server-side logs for those req ids and the rerun count. Also, are these calls to /v1/embeddings or /v1/rerank?

laura_support: embeddings endpoint. Customer code snippet in ticket: 
```python
from tenacity import retry, wait_exponential
@retry(wait=wait_exponential(multiplier=1, max=60))
def push_batch(batch):
    resp = requests.post('https://api.redwood.ai/v1/embeddings', json=batch, headers=headers)
    resp.raise_for_status()
    return resp.json()
```
They said they don't set any idempotency key on retries.

ingest-bot: automated-log: matched 3 request_ids for acct_9XY. total_tokens: 921k across requests. server-retries-triggered: 14 for those ids. upstream-status-codes: 200(15), 429(9), 500(2). full events: https://internal-logs/redwood/1771234567 (restricted)

sam_ops: 14 server retries looks suspicious. Are retries happening client-side and server-side duplicate processing is not deduped?

jihoon_eng: on embeddings we historically didn't require idempotency-key for token charging. If a client retries and server reprocesses, tokens are charged each successful call. Need to confirm whether our server retried a downstream model call and then recharged on success.

marta_billing: tagging billing — if this is true we should consider a refund for the excess consumption. Can someone produce a minimal repro and timeline so we can calculate the refund amount?

laura_support: customer willing to share a sanitized sample job. I'll request the job config + manifest and ask them to run a single-batch test with idempotency header omitted/added.

jihoon_eng: quick checklist for root cause: 1) check API gateway logs for duplicate acceptances (same client-sent body, different request ids) 2) check backend model invocation trace to see if we retried downstream kernel and recharged 3) check our retry policy when response is 429 vs. 500.

sam_ops: we should also check autoscaling/queued batches — if load spikes we might have requeued same batch and processed twice. I'll look at queue ack semantics.

marta_billing: provisional action: issue a temporary credit to acct_9XY for the visible spike while eng investigates. I'll hold on final refund until we have the exact count.

laura_support: got a quick response from the customer: they see idempotency not set and their client retries on any exception. They attached logs showing sequential requests ~every 30s when they got 429.

jihoon_eng: if customer retries on 429 and our upstream returns 429 during model cold-start, that could produce multiple accepted requests once model becomes available. We need to treat 429 as potentially non-idempotent or ensure idempotency keys dedupe.

sam_ops: workaround for customers: 1) set Idempotency-Key header per logical batch 2) use our client SDK which sets idempotency by default for batch endpoints 3) tune retry to avoid re-sending until after a longer backoff or use 429-specific handling.

laura_support: I'll share those mitigation suggestions with the customer and ask for the sample run. Also asked them to confirm whether promo code was applied before or after the spike — they said promo applied at 00:05Z and spike starts 00:30Z.

marta_billing: noted. We'll queue a provisional credit for now (small amount) and reconcile after eng confirms the exact double-processed count.

jihoon_eng: created ENG ticket ENG-1198 to investigate idempotency behavior on embeddings endpoint and whether gateway is assigning new request ids when retries come from same client. Assigned to me.

laura_support: customer appreciates the quick help. I'll update the support ticket with the temporary credit and the recommended steps. If eng finds a server bug we'll coordinate a full refund and a postmortem. :thumbsup:

sam_ops: FYI I'm also adding a short alert to the ingest queue dashboard to highlight sudden token burn spikes so we can catch these faster.

marta_billing: thanks all. keep me posted on ENG-1198 timeline and final numbers.

jihoon_eng: will update in this thread when I have the trace. likely ETA 24-48h.

laura_support: closing the slack thread and moving details to the support ticket + ENG-1198. leaving this here for audit.

ingest-bot: note: alert created -> ingest-token-burn-high, threshold 20k tokens/min.

laura_support: (also added snippet to the support reply showing how to add header)

laura_support: Example header for idempotency: `Idempotency-Key: <uuid4>`
